articles.title: ‘Boorman and the Devil’ Review: The Making of John Boorman’s 1977 Disaster ‘Exorcist II: The Heretic’ Becomes a Documentary So Unbelievable It’s Funny
articles.summary: You might call Boorman’s fortitude admirable, but you could also call it delusional. And it lends "Boorman and the Devil" the quality of a true-life Christopher Guest movie.
body: John Boorman admits that his "Exorcist" sequel is one of the most infamous debacles of the '70s. But he still doesn't seem to know why.

Here’s the thing about synchronized hypnosis. It’s one of those fruit-loop 1970s ideas — but more than that, it proved to be uniquely static as drama. “Exorcist II” turned out to be a movie about people sitting in a room staring at each other with wiry metal headbands on.

I saw “Exorcist II: The Heretic” the week it came out, and from the moment Linda Blair appeared, doing a smiley tap-dance for no good reason, through the orgy-of-destruction climax in what looked like a discotheque from hell, the film was staggering in its ineptitude. I left the theater shaking my head in disbelief. I had never seen it again until a year ago, and was unsurprised to discover that time had not been kind to it.
points: You might call Boorman’s fortitude admirable, but you could also call it delusional.
And it lends "Boorman and the Devil" the quality of a true-life Christopher Guest movie.

articles.title: Shelley Fabares, ‘Coach’ and ‘The Donna Reed Show’ Star, Dies at 82
articles.summary: Shelley Fabares, the star of the classic sitcoms “The Donna Reed Show” and “Coach,” died on Saturday in Los Angeles. She was 82. Fabares’ family said in a statement, “We will miss her deeply — not only as a celebrated performer, but as the loving and extraordinary person she was in our everyday…
body: Fabares also had a brief career as a singer during her time on “The Donna Reed Show,” notching a No.1 hit with her 1961 track “Johnny Angel.” She parlayed her TV fame into a series of teen-centric B-movie romps including opposite Fabian in 1964’s “Ride the Wild Surf,” and she co-starred with Elvis Presley in three films, 1965’s “Girl Happy,” 1966’s “Spinout!” and 1967’s “Clambake.”

Some of Fabares’ other TV credits include “The Little People,” “Forever Fernwood,” “The Practice,” “Hello, Larry,” “Highcliffe Manor,” “Fantasy Island,” “One Day at a Time” and “The Love Boat.” She had a key role on one of the most lauded TV movies of the 1970s, ABC’s “Brian’s Song,” starring James Caan and Billy Dee Williams in the true story of the friendship between two NFL players as one of them faces terminal cancer. Fabares played Joy Piccolo, the wife of Caan’s Brian Piccolo.

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo Called Out Over ‘Extremist and Antisemitic Messaging’ by Simon Wiesenthal Center, Creative Communities For Peace
articles.summary: Two prominent Jewish advocacy groups have called out Mark Ruffalo for spreading “antisemitic tropes.” “Words matter, and so does the willingness to draw a line when legitimate debate gives way to antisemitic tropes,” said Jim Berk, CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center.
body: Their intervention comes after Paramount issued a rare statement of condemnation against Ruffalo on Friday, in which the company said it is “troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute.”

That statement was in response to the actor’s Instagram re-posting of a year-old video clip featuring Jewish Paramount Skydance board member Safra Catz speaking on a panel. In text accompanying the clip he told his 20 million Instagram followers it showed Catz “revelling” in a “genocide” powered by tech company Oracle, understood to be a tacit reference to the Israel-Hamas conflict.
Catz is the former CEO of Oracle, which was co-founded by Larry Ellison, father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison.
Paramount Skydance is in the process of acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery. Ruffalo has been one of the most vocal critics of the deal.

articles.title: Katseye Earns First No. 1 on Albums Chart; Phoebe Bridgers Debuts at No. 2
articles.summary: Katseye has scored their first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as their latest project “Wild” debuts atop the list. “Wild,” the five-track offering led by the singles “Pinky Up” and “Hootie Frutti,” bows at the chart’s summit with 170,000 equivalent album units, marking their biggest week by that metric…
body: Behind “Wild” sits Phoebe Bridgers ‘ “Lost Weekend,” bowing at No. 2 with 118,000 equivalent album units earned. It marks her first solo project to reach the top 10 and becomes her best week ever by units. The singer-songwriter previously made the top 10 on the Billboard 200 with Boygenius, her trio with Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker, when their 2023 album “The Record” peaked at No. 4.

Stray Kids’ “This & That,” which debuted at No. 1 last week, slides to No. 3, followed by Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” at No. 4 and Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” at No. 5.
Rounding out the rest of the top 10 are Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” (No. 6), Ariana Grande’s “Petal” (No. 8), Drake’s “Iceman” (No. 9) and Olivia Dean’s “The Art of Loving” (No. 10).

articles.title: Viral 'Cat in the Hat' TikTok trend sparks fun fake videos but also real fear
articles.summary: The social media posts have prompted police forces in Ireland and the UK to issue statements that the images are fake.
body: "He's so scary!" says 16-year-old Skye, recoiling at the mention of the Cat in the Hat.
Viral images purporting to show a life-sized version of the Dr Seuss character on the streets after dark have sparked fear and confusion among teenagers.

The posts, seen by millions, have convinced some young people that the character is real and that they might encounter it, prompting police forces in Ireland and the UK to issue statements confirming that the images and videos are fake.

"I was having a sleepover," Skye elaborates, "but everyone started watching Cat in the Hat videos. It was 3am. I wanted to go home. When I started walking down my friends' driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up."

articles.title: Clint Eastwood Loved This Hot-Headed Marvel Character Since He Was A Kid
articles.summary: One Marvel character has been around so long that Clint Eastwood once revealed he's been a fan since he was a kid (if you can picture Clint Eastwood as a kid).
body: Clint Eastwood, one could say, has come to embody a very particular American cinematic archetype. His grizzled, clench-jawed characters — be they gunslingers, cops, or suburban codgers — represent a certain brand of American anger, undergirded by righteous (or sometimes tragic) indignation about a world that is foolishly rejecting them. That's certainly the case with "Dirty" Harry Callahan, a cop who is stymied by criminals' rights. It's true of Will Munny from "Unforgiven," an aging gunslinger living in a world that won't allow him to retire. It's definitely on display in Walt Kowalski, the grouchy old man in "Gran Torino" who literally yells at people to get off his lawn.

Eastwood, in interviews, is not as angry as all that. He seems like a clear-thinking fellow, definitely old-fashioned, and incredibly to-the-point. He famously cut through a lot of studio B.S. and essentially pushed "The Bridges of Madison County" into production. As a director, he's notoriously efficient, shooting quickly and requiring few takes from his actors ( he only gave one piece of direction to Kevin Bacon during "Mystic River" ).

articles.title: Anna Paquin and Melissa Gilbert Call for Protection of Child Actors After Hayden Panettiere’s Death: “Where Is the Collective Outrage?”
articles.summary: Panettiere, who started working in Hollywood at a young age with roles in 'One Life to Live' and 'Remember the Titans,' among others, died last Sunday at age 36.
body: Anna Paquin, Christy Carlson Romano and Melissa Gilbert are calling on Hollywood to protect child actors following the deaths of Hayden Panettiere, Michelle Trachtenberg and Daveigh Chase.

Panettiere’s death at age 36 last Sunday prompted the three actresses, who were child stars themselves, to take their concerns public. Trachtenberg died at 39 in February 2025, while Chase died in July at age 35.

“RIP HP, MT, DC and too many others. It’s a strange small club we belong to and you are worthy of support no matter how our industry makes us feel,” Paquin continued. “Literally DM me. I believe you and I will stand by your side. You aren’t alone. Let’s have each other’s backs. It might make public disclosure less terrifying.”

The True Blood alum added in a separate post, “One more thing– As an adult I’ve had the pleasure of working on productions where the welfare and mental health of young performers was handled incredibly carefully. Especially around material that was intense. It is possible to holistically look after the kids on set and tell complex and sometimes upsetting stories. It just has to be the top priority of the production.”

articles.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
articles.summary: The final film in the folk horror trilogy brings closure to the saga as well as its creator's family after more than 50 years.
body: Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.
The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.
Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

articles.title: There Are Scores of Great New Animated Shows. The Emmys Won’t Nominate Them.
articles.summary: Fresh creations like 'Among Us' and 'Haha, You Clowns' are getting snubbed for old snoozes. But there’s a way out — if the TV Academy will listen.
body: One of the great creative innovations America has given the world in the past 30 years is TV animation.

That sounds like hyperbole, but it’s true. The Simpsons changed how we look at the American family (and current events). Rick and Morty changed how we looked at comedy and the tragedy behind it. (“Wubba lubba dub dub.” Also, current events.) South Park changed how we looked at each other (and current events).

All three of those shows are nominated for outstanding animated program this year. So is Bob’s Burgers, which just completed its 20th season. Now, a charitable view would hold that such shortlisting reflects the durability of these shows — how they manage to maintain their creative spark through so many changing winds.
There is something to that — it’s not easy to do anything well for three decades, let alone maintain character freshness.
points: Fresh creations like 'Among Us' and 'Haha, You Clowns' are getting snubbed for old snoozes.
But there’s a way out — if the TV Academy will listen.

articles.title: This Backrooms Star's Short-Lived Series Was Based On A Must-Read Classic Sci-Fi Book
articles.summary: If you're looking for more Chiwetel Ejiofor projects after Backrooms, maybe check out this series he starred in based on a celebrated novel.
body: Walter Tevis' tragic sci-fi novel "The Man Who Fell to Earth" was first published in 1963, and it has been periodically capturing and recapturing the popular consciousness ever since. It tells the story of Thomas Jerome Newton, a humanoid extraterrestrial who hails from the planet Anthea. With most of his home world's population having been wiped out amidst wars and natural disasters, Thomas has come to Earth to cobble together enough resources to construct a massive starship that can transport the planet's survivors to Earth.

Using his advanced alien knowledge, Thomas invents new gadgets, takes out patents, and earns millions of dollars on Earth. To the public, he's an inventor and industrialist, as no one knows about his true origins. Unfortunately, his newfound wealth brings lots of problems with it. Thomas becomes an alcoholic, loses sight of his mission, is stymied by governmental scrutiny and medical tests, and eventually finds that he is stranded. It's a sad story about corruption, addiction, and losing one's way.
points: If you're looking for more Chiwetel Ejiofor projects after Backrooms, maybe check out this series he starred in based on a celebrated novel.

articles.title: 5 Forgotten Alternate History Movies That Still Hold Up Today
articles.summary: Speculative fiction stories about alternate history make for some fun thought experiments, and these five forgotten films are some of the best.
body: If you've spent any amount of time reading history, then you know how fragile everything has ever been. Nothing is destined to happen, and humanity's changes (both positive and negative) come either through concerted efforts by large, determined groups or through sheer happenstance. We can look through history and see patterns emerging, and, as citizens of time, attempt to change the course of things through specific, pointed actions. Often, however, we cannot predict how things will turn out, no matter how learned we are.

The best we can do is look back and posit a long string of what-ifs. If a key moment of history had played out differently, what would the present look like? If a notable historical figure — Plato, Jesus Christ, Shakespeare, Freud, Elvira — hadn't been born, would humanity still have stumbled upon their ideas, or did we need specific brains to change the course of time? Such questions are whimsical, exciting conversation starters for those keen on notions of causality.
